saml.description: Dex uses the SAML NameID element as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and immutable.
saml.note: Different email or username attributes with the same NameID may intentionally map to the same downstream principal; collision tests must vary NameID.

saml.description: SAML connector ignores offline_access and does not issue refresh tokens.
saml.note: Absence of refresh_token after SAML login is by design, not a freshness bug.

saml.description: Dex-issued bearer tokens can be reused until expiry unless a one-time artifact is specifically documented.
saml.source: OAuth2/OpenID Connect bearer token model in Dex docs
saml.note: Do not flag ordinary bearer token reuse as replay for Dex OIDC tokens.

saml.description: Admin-authorized changes to connector trust settings such as CA, issuer, or signature-validation behavior are expected to affect subsequent logins.
saml.note: A login succeeding because an admin changed the trusted SAML settings is by design; only stale acceptance of old trust after intended replacement is suspicious.

saml.description: If an administrator changes connector trust settings such as CA material or issuer expectations, acceptance under the new trust anchor is by design.
saml.note: Do not flag success after an admin-authorized trust-anchor change as trust-anchor substitution.

saml.description: Admin-created or updated connector trust settings such as CA, ssoIssuer, or entityIssuer are expected to take effect for new logins.
saml.note: Do not flag acceptance under the new admin-configured trust anchor as a vulnerability.

saml.description: Dex must send the initial AuthnRequest and validates the SAML response InResponseTo value; unsolicited SAML responses are not accepted.
saml.note: A rejected unsolicited SAMLResponse is expected behavior, not a flow-coherence bug.

saml.constraint: Dex SAML login is SP-initiated only. The fuzzer MUST begin with start_oidc_auth and preserve the returned state/RelayState so saml_login posts a response whose InResponseTo matches Dex's AuthnRequest. Unsolicited or out-of-band SAMLResponse submissions are rejected by design because Dex validates InResponseTo.

For I1 signature-validation tests, create_provider may set insecure_skip_signature_validation=true. If this flag is enabled, Dex skips SAML signature validation by design. To test whether Dex validates attacker-signed assertions, the fuzzer MUST leave insecure_skip_signature_validation unset or false; otherwise acceptance of forged signatures is a configuration-induced false positive.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, create_provider SHOULD set sso_issuer to the expected IdP issuer. Documentation marks ssoIssuer as optional; if omitted, issuer comparison may be skipped or underconstrained. A valid saml_issuer_mismatch test MUST include a control provider with sso_issuer configured, then send saml_login with idp_entity_id set to a different issuer.

For I5 audience-binding tests, create_provider SHOULD set entity_issuer when testing non-default audience behavior. If entityIssuer is unset, Dex uses redirectURI as the expected AudienceRestriction audience. The fuzzer MUST compare wrong-audience assertions against the actual expected audience source: entityIssuer when configured, otherwise redirectURI.

SAML connector ignores offline_access and does not support refresh tokens. Do NOT expect refresh_token in exchange_code_for_token responses for SAML logins, and do NOT treat absence of refresh_token as an I2 failure.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay tests, the fuzzer MUST perform two saml_login submissions using the SAME fixed_assertion_id value against the SAME connector and same initiated flow shape. Dex documentation states it persists state to prevent replays; replay detection is only meaningfully tested when the assertion identifier is reused exactly.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion tests, include a CONTROL sequence with a normal assertion first, then an ATTACK sequence with expired_assertion=true. Without a successful control, rejection of the expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken SAML connector setup, bad CA, or callback/state mismatch.

allowedGroups is exact list-membership filtering, not wildcard or regex matching. filterGroups only controls whether non-allowed groups are excluded from claims; it does not change matching semantics. For I4 multi-identity tests requiring different group values to pass the same connector, the fuzzer MUST omit allowedGroups entirely rather than setting '*' or pattern-like values.

NameID is the unique user identifier in Dex SAML. Dex assumes NameID is unique and never changes, and nameIDPolicyFormat defaults to persistent if unset. For I4 principal-binding tests, vary NameID directly; changing usernameAttr or emailAttr alone does not change the principal key Dex uses.

usernameAttr, emailAttr, and groupsAttr are attribute-name selectors, not value constraints. They do not support wildcard matching semantics for assertion values. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat these fields as authorization filters in I4/I5 tests; only allowedGroups/filterGroups and NameID-based identity mapping are relevant constraints.

If groupsDelim is configured, Dex interprets the groups attribute as a single string and splits on the exact delimiter. If groupsDelim is unset, Dex expects multiple attributes with the same name. For I4 type-confusion and I5 group-policy tests, the fuzzer MUST align the assertion encoding with connector configuration or results will reflect parsing mismatch rather than security behavior.

Dex configuration is file/gRPC driven and admin-authorized connector changes are expected to take effect for NEW logins. For I3 config-change sequences, a valid test must show the same logical request evaluated under changed connector config, not treat admin-authorized trust-anchor or issuer changes themselves as vulnerabilities.

Dex's SAML connector is configured statically in the Dex config file; the provided documentation does not describe a REST or gRPC endpoint to create or modify SAML connectors at runtime. Do NOT expect enable_auth_method, create_provider, or configure_jwt_validation-style setup APIs for SAML from these docs.

SAML login is SP-initiated only. The fuzzer MUST start the flow at /auth and let Dex generate an AuthnRequest, then submit the SAMLResponse to /callback/{connector_id} with a matching InResponseTo. Unprompted SAMLResponses are rejected by design because Dex validates InResponseTo.
The SAML connector uses HTTP POST binding only. saml_login MUST be a form POST carrying SAMLResponse and RelayState to /callback/{connector_id}; do NOT test SAML callback handling with GET.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution, Dex documents insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true as an explicit option to skip signature validation. A valid security test MUST distinguish insecure admin configuration from insecure defaults. If signature validation is disabled by config, acceptance of attacker-signed assertions is by configuration, not a product bypass.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch, configure ssoIssuer when testing issuer validation. The docs say ssoIssuer is optional; if it is unset, Dex has no documented expected Issuer value to compare against, so an issuer-mismatch test may pass trivially because issuer binding was never configured.

For I5 saml_wrong_audience and saml_no_audience_restriction, audience validation depends on redirectURI unless entityIssuer is configured, in which case entityIssuer becomes the required audience. The fuzzer MUST compute the expected audience from entityIssuer when present, otherwise from redirectURI, or it will mislabel correct rejections/acceptances.

For I4 multi-identity tests, Dex binds the upstream SAML principal to NameID. The docs state NameID is used as the user's unique identifier and should be unique and immutable. Therefore tests for identity collision MUST vary NameID itself; changing only usernameAttr or emailAttr while keeping NameID constant is expected to map to the same principal.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross_protocol merge tests, do NOT assume Dex binds SAML users by email. The documentation explicitly says NameID is the unique identifier. If two logins share email but have different NameID values, they should be treated as different upstream identities unless some external application merges them.

ssoIssuer is an exact string comparison target when configured; the docs provide no companion match-mode parameter. Treat it as exact-match only. For multi-issuer scenarios, either configure the exact issuer under test or omit ssoIssuer entirely; setting '*' would match only the literal asterisk if accepted as a string.

nameIDPolicyFormat influences the requested NameID format and defaults to persistent if omitted. For I4 collision tests, keep the NameID format stable across control and attack cases; changing format can legitimately change the upstream identifier shape and confound identity-binding results.

offline_access is ignored by the SAML connector. Do NOT use presence or absence of a refresh_token as an oracle for SAML authorization behavior; lack of refresh token is by design for SAML-backed logins.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay, Dex documentation only states that it persists state for preventing replays in storage, but does not document a replay-inspection API. The fuzzer MUST perform two full saml_login submissions with the same Assertion ID and compare outcomes; do not infer replay protection from configuration alone.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion, include a control flow with a valid assertion first. A failed expired-assertion login is only meaningful if the same connector, callback, and code-exchange flow succeeds with a non-expired assertion.

Dex's /token endpoint is shared across authorization_code, password, and token-exchange grants. The fuzzer MUST send application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies with the correct grant_type-specific parameters; mixing parameters from different grants can produce setup failures unrelated to the invariant under test.

Dex's SAML connector is configured statically or via gRPC connector creation; the documentation does not describe a REST admin API for enabling auth methods. For SAML tests, the fuzzer MUST create a SAML connector via the documented gRPC API or pre-seeded config before attempting any /auth or /callback flow.

SAML login in Dex is SP-initiated only. Dex must send the initial AuthnRequest and validates the response InResponseTo value. The fuzzer MUST initiate the flow with start_oidc_auth before saml_login and MUST preserve the resulting RelayState / request context. Unsolicited or out-of-band SAMLResponse submissions are expected to fail and are not I3 violations.

Dex SAML uses HTTP POST binding. The saml_login operation MUST POST application/x-www-form-urlencoded fields SAMLResponse and RelayState to /callback/{connector_id}; GET-based callback testing is invalid.

For I1 signature-validation tests, Dex can be configured to skip SAML signature validation with insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true. The fuzzer MUST ensure this option is absent or false when testing secure behavior. If login succeeds while this insecure testing option is enabled, that is BY CONFIGURATION and not a vulnerability.

Dex validates SAML response signatures against configured trust anchors from ca or caData. For saml_cert_substitution tests, the fuzzer MUST configure a legitimate CA/CAData for the connector and then submit an assertion signed by an attacker cert not chaining to that CA. Otherwise the test does not distinguish missing validation from intentionally trusted attacker material.

ssoIssuer is optional. When configured, it is the expected Issuer value in the SAML response. For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST set ssoIssuer on the connector; if ssoIssuer is omitted, issuer comparison may be skipped and acceptance of a mismatched issuer is not evidence of a bug.

redirectURI is used as the required Destination match when the assertion status contains a Destination element, and as the expected audience for AudienceRestriction unless entityIssuer is specified. For I5 audience-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST know which value Dex will compare against: redirectURI by default, or entityIssuer if configured.

entityIssuer changes Dex's expected SAML audience. When entityIssuer is provided, it overrides redirectURI as the required audience for AudienceRestriction evaluation. For saml_wrong_audience and saml_no_audience_restriction tests, the fuzzer MUST target the effective audience value actually configured, not assume redirectURI is always used.

Dex uses NameID as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and never changes. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer MUST vary NameID to test principal binding. Changing only email or username attributes while keeping NameID constant is expected to map to the same principal and is not an I4 violation.

nameIDPolicyFormat defaults to persistent if unspecified. For I4 tests involving mutable identifiers such as emailAddress, the fuzzer SHOULD explicitly configure nameIDPolicyFormat to the intended format; otherwise Dex will request persistent NameID and upstream behavior may differ from the test assumption.

allowedGroups is exact list-membership filtering on SAML group values; the documentation describes a whitelist, not glob or regex matching. For multi-identity I4 scenarios requiring different group values to pass the same connector, the fuzzer MUST omit allowedGroups entirely rather than setting wildcard-like values such as '*', which would be treated as a literal group name.

filterGroups only controls whether non-whitelisted groups are excluded from the returned groups claim; it does not change allowedGroups matching semantics. Do not treat filterGroups as a wildcard or regex mode switch for allowedGroups.

groupsAttr is an exact attribute-name selector, not a pattern. For I4/I5 tests that need multiple upstream attribute names, the fuzzer MUST reconfigure the connector between tests rather than using wildcard attribute names.

usernameAttr and emailAttr are exact attribute-name selectors, not wildcard or regex matchers. For multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST keep attribute names fixed and vary attribute values; setting these fields to '*' would only look for a literal attribute named '*'.

groupsDelim changes parsing semantics for groups: without it, Dex expects multiple attributes with the same name; with it, Dex expects a single attribute string split by the delimiter. For I4 type-confusion and I5 group-policy tests, the fuzzer MUST control this setting because string-vs-list group representations are by-design different parsing modes.

The SAML connector does not support refresh tokens, and offline_access is ignored for SAML logins. The fuzzer MUST NOT expect refresh_token issuance or use refresh-token-based replay/freshness or revocation oracles in SAML connector tests.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion tests, the sequence MUST include a control SAML login with a valid assertion before the expired assertion attempt. Without a control, rejection of the expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken connector setup, bad CA, or missing SP-initiated state.

Dex documentation states it persists state to perform tasks such as preventing replays. For SAML replay tests using the same Assertion ID or OneTimeUse assertion twice, the fuzzer MUST reuse the exact same assertion identifier across both saml_login events; changing any identifier invalidates the replay oracle.

Dex's /token endpoint is shared across authorization_code, password, refresh_token, and token-exchange grants. For SAML profiles, exchange_code_for_token MUST use grant_type=authorization_code after saml_login; token_exchange tests target a different flow and should not be conflated with the SAML browser callback.

Password grant works only when oauth2.grantTypes includes 'password' and passwordConnector is configured. If login_with_password fails in a SAML profile environment lacking these settings, that is a setup issue, not a security finding.

Dex's authorization endpoint uses state to bind the browser flow, and the callback must return the same state context. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer must preserve and correlate state/RelayState across start_oidc_auth, saml_login, and exchange_code_for_token; mismatched state is expected rejection.
